notes: page_size raised from 100 to 1000 (measured 2026-09-30): the API answers 1000 rows in 9.6s versus 8.5s for 100, so a full history walk of ledger 1 (573,553 rows) is ~574 requests instead of ~5,740 and draws far less of the shared rate limit. The key includes module: batch numbers are per module, so a GL, AP or CA batch can share batchNumber and lineNumber with another (Consult AS returned 4 such pairs among 120,651 rows, measured 2026-10-01, and the sync rejected them as duplicate primary keys). The pilot tenant has none, so [batchNumber, lineNumber] passed there. Walked one financial period at a time (period_scan, resume): the old walk of ledger 1 by lastModifiedDateTime alone read the pilot's 575,000 lines as 575 pages of 1,000, and on 2026-10-02 three full runs ended on HTTP 500 'Execution Timeout Expired' at deep pages (the server's own query limit; the slowest page was 48 s on 09-30). fromPeriod/toPeriod give the same rows at about 2 s a page (26,457 lines in 202609), and the API accepts lastModifiedDateTime on top of them, so a scheduled run asks each period only for what changed since its checkpoint (2,030 of 26,457 lines for one day) and a full pass asks for everything. look_ahead_months 12 reaches periods posted ahead of time.
